what: First American Financial sells title insurance. When a property changes hands in the United States, someone must verify that the seller actually owns it free of liens and claims; First American searches the records, insures against errors and handles the closing and escrow.
customers: Homebuyers, mortgage lenders, commercial property investors and the real estate agents and attorneys who manage transactions. It also sells data and settlement services to lenders.
money: Premiums on residential and commercial title policies, plus escrow and closing fees.
Home warranty products, and its banking and investment operations.
moat: Title insurance rests on owning the records. First American has assembled a vast database of historical property records across the United States, which lowers the cost of each search and is not reproducible. Rates are regulated state by state, and the handful of national underwriters have held their positions for decades.
risks: Revenue follows housing transaction volume, which fell sharply with mortgage rates: from $9.2B in 2021 to $6.0B in 2023 before recovering to $7.5B.
Mortgage rates, not anything management controls, determine how many houses change hands and therefore how many policies are written.
Commercial property transactions are lumpy and have been weak, and they carry the highest premiums per deal.
The company has had a significant information security incident in the past, and it holds large volumes of sensitive personal and financial data.
Only five analysts cover the stock, so the $79.00 average target rests on few opinions.
opportunities: The shares trade at about 9.0 times earnings, 0.81 times sales and 3.7 times EV/EBITDA, cheap for a business with these barriers to entry.
Free cash flow of $805.8M against a $6.5B market value is a very large yield.
Cash of about $1.4B dwarfs debt of $218.2M, and the investment portfolio earns more as interest rates stay high.
A fall in mortgage rates would restart transaction volumes quickly, and the operating leverage in title insurance is considerable.
watch: Existing home sales volume. Title insurance revenue is almost a direct function of how many properties change hands, so that national figure tells you more about the next quarter than anything the company says.
